Eltharn SOCKS5 client compatibility adapter
==========================================

This directory contains an original, narrow compatibility adapter written for
Eltharn. Its package name satisfies the dependency interface used by Azalea;
it is not a fork, vendored copy or relicensing of the GPL socks5-impl package.
No implementation bodies from that package were used to write this adapter.
The original adapter is covered by the project license at ../../../LICENSE.

Reviewed consumer:
https://github.com/azalea-rs/azalea/blob/41a9ae6aaff77646c08c64ac1334a8cc6081c24f/azalea-protocol/src/connect.rs

The supported interface is protocol::UserKey, its public username/password
fields and constructor, Clone/Debug/Display, and client::connect on a fresh
tokio::io::BufStream<tokio::net::TcpStream> with a SocketAddr destination.
The Azalea consumer discards connect's success value. No server, BIND, UDP,
GSSAPI or general drop-in compatibility with socks5-impl is claimed.

Public interface reference, consulted without reading implementation bodies:
https://docs.rs/socks5-impl/0.8.7/socks5_impl/protocol/handshake/password_method/struct.UserKey.html

Wire behavior is delegated to the separately licensed tokio-socks crate:
https://github.com/sticnarf/tokio-socks
https://docs.rs/tokio-socks/0.5.3/tokio_socks/tcp/struct.Socks5Stream.html

SOCKS5 CONNECT and username/password negotiation are specified by RFC 1928 and
RFC 1929. These are network protocol contracts, not Minecraft behavior rules.
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1928.html
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1929.html

The actual caller creates an empty BufStream immediately before negotiation
and extracts its TcpStream immediately afterward. The adapter therefore uses
the underlying TcpStream for the handshake, avoiding buffered writes and
read-ahead that could discard the first destination bytes on into_inner().
It must not be called on a BufStream with existing buffered reads or writes.
The direct-server connection route is outside this adapter and is unchanged.

Display produces percent-encoded URI credentials for Azalea's reqwest proxy
conversion. Debug redacts both fields. Display output contains credentials
and must not be logged. It is not an engine account/session storage service.

Runtime dependencies retain their own licenses: tokio-socks (MIT), Tokio
(MIT), percent-encoding (MIT OR Apache-2.0), and their resolved dependencies.
Include their required notices in distributed dependency attribution.
